version.changelog:
Initial release: Playwright-based browser automation skill, fully independent of DuMate.

- Provides a CLI tool (`pw-browser`) for browser automation using Playwright with Node.js, supporting all key actions like navigation, snap, click, fill, scroll, and tab management.
- No DuMate agent or extension required—runs standalone, using system-installed Chrome or Edge (via Playwright channel).
- Includes robust session/daemon management for persistent browser/browser state across commands.
- Detailed semantic rules and workflow best practices are documented, ensuring reliable usage patterns.
- Command overview and advanced strategies (wait, snap, run-code, pagination, SPA handling) included.

llm.summary: This is a real browser automation skill, but it exposes unchecked custom Playwright code and live page-changing actions that deserve review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Node and Playwright are proportionate to the purpose, but allowed Bash curl access is not clearly used, and the local HTTP daemon exposes broad browser/session control to any local process that can call 127.0.0.1:19223.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal npm-based Node setup, but package.json uses a ranged Playwright dependency and no lockfile was present, reducing reproducibility for a browser-driving tool.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include custom code execution, form submission, downloads, and save/update/publish workflows without strong confirmation, dry-run, or domain scoping guidance for live accounts and persistent content changes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon persists for the session, keeps browser/page state across commands, and writes ~/.pw-browser/daemon.json; this is documented and has close/shutdown commands, but users should treat the live session as privileged.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser automation purpose is coherent, and the skill discloses daemon-based Playwright control, screenshots, eval, and run-code, but run-code is an unrestricted Playwright Page escape hatch over the active browser session.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the publisher and need a high-trust browser automation tool. Use it in a separate browser profile where possible, close the daemon after use, avoid running run-code/eval from untrusted prompts, and require dependency pinning or an updated Playwright version before broad deployment.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded from deception: the SKILL.md does disclose the daemon, persistent browser state, and eval/run-code, though the metadata description is narrower than the effective authority.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a review concern: SKILL.md and references/running-code.md present arbitrary Playwright code execution as a normal advanced feature, without bounded operations or opt-in warnings.
[SDI-1] expected: Accepted as a review concern: pw-browser.js implements eval and new Function('page', ...) against the active Playwright page, giving arbitrary automation control over authenticated browser state.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: examples for rich-text editing, save/publish actions, downloads, and form submission can modify remote or local state, but the artifacts do not add strong user-confirmation or reversibility guidance.
[SC1] unexpected: Accepted as a supply-chain note: package.json uses "playwright": "^1.51.0" and no lockfile was present in the inspected artifact.
[SC4] unexpected: Accepted as a review note based on the supplied scanner signal and matching dependency range in package.json; users should require a patched, pinned Playwright version before installation.
